request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 
The 53-year-old male with a history of pleural effusion and cardiac dysfunction who underwent video-assisted empyema curettage under sedation with DEX and regional anesthesia is now being discharged from the hospital.

Hospital Course:
The patient was monitored for cardiac arrest and had DOB administered prior to surgery due to cardiac dysfunction. The surgery was performed under regional anesthesia with lidocaine and fentanyl administered for pain. The operative time was 37 minutes, and the anesthetic time was 59 minutes. After surgery, the patient was fully awake and returned to the ICU without oxygen supplementation. The patient was moved out of the ICU on POD 1 and had no complications due to anesthesia. The patient was discharged from hospital on POD 19.

Medications:
No medication details were given in the case report. 

Follow-up Care:
The patient was followed up without any problems, and no further follow-up care was mentioned in the case report. 
Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
The patient underwent video-assisted empyema curettage under sedation with DEX and regional anesthesia. Lidocaine and fentanyl were used for pain as required.

Discharge Condition:
Stable condition.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The patient had video-assisted curettage of an empyema, so the condition chiefly responsible for the admission is empyema, meaning pus in the pleural cavity. In ICD-10, J86 is pyothorax and covers empyema, with J86.0 for pyothorax with fistula and J86.9 for pyothorax without fistula. The cardiac dysfunction and the pleural effusion history are secondary to this.

The summary does not name an organism, so I did not use a code for a specific infective cause, such as pneumonia with empyema (J85/J18) or a bacterial code. J86 is the best fit for the information given.

CODE: J86
